readmeHtml:
Documentation | Changelog | Roadmap

The web has evolved. Finally, testing has too.

Fast, easy and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser.

Join us, we're hiring.


What is Cypress?

Installing

Install Cypress for Mac, Linux, or Windows, then get started.

npm install cypress --save-dev

or

yarn add cypress --dev

or

pnpm add cypress --save-dev

Contributing

- develop branch

Please see our Contributing Guideline which explains repo organization, linting, testing, and other steps.

License

This project is licensed under the terms of the MIT license.

Badges

Configure a badge for your project's README to show your test status or test count in the Cypress Cloud.

Or let the world know your project is using Cypress with the badge below.

[![Cypress.io](https://img.shields.io/badge/tested%20with-Cypress-04C38E.svg)](https://www.cypress.io/)

aiSummary.oneLiner: Fast, reliable, and easy-to-use testing tool tailored for anything that runs in a web browser.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Cypress is a next-generation front-end testing tool built for the modern web. Unlike Selenium-based tools, Cypress executes directly in the same run-loop as the application, allowing it to provide native access to the DOM, network traffic, and local storage. It enables developers to write end-to-end tests, integration tests, and unit tests with a time-traveling UI that shows exactly what happened at each step. Cypress automatically waits for elements to appear and network requests to finish, eliminating the need for manual waits and reducing test flakiness.
keyFeatures: In-browser execution: Runs in the same run-loop as the application, providing native access to everything in the browser.
Time travel debugging: Takes snapshots as tests run, allowing developers to hover over commands in the Command Log to see the UI state at that exact moment.
Automatic waiting: Never requires explicit waits or sleeps; it automatically waits for commands and assertions before moving on.
Network traffic control: Easily stubs and mocks edge cases by controlling, stubbing, and testing network requests without hitting the server.
Real-time reloads: Automatically reloads whenever changes are made to test files, optimizing the TDD workflow.

useCases.title: End-to-end testing
useCases.description: QA engineers write tests that simulate complete user journeys, from logging in to completing a purchase.

useCases.title: Component testing
useCases.description: Frontend developers mount and test individual React, Vue, or Angular components in isolation using the real browser DOM.

useCases.title: Network mocking
useCases.description: Developers stub API responses to test how the frontend handles specific error states or edge case data without backend dependencies.

useCases.title: CI integration
useCases.description: DevOps teams run headless Cypress tests in GitHub Actions to block deployments if core application flows break.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Cypress is designed for frontend developers and QA engineers who build and test modern web applications. It requires Node.js and integrates easily into standard JavaScript projects.
